evidence.title: Multi-agent traces reveal distinct failure modes and verification gaps
evidence.observation: Authors classify 1,642 traces from seven engineered multi-agent frameworks into 14 failure modes. Missing information can reflect withholding, ignored input, or context failure. Verification flaws also occur in successful runs.
evidence.evidence_standing: Bounded observation (researcher-reported experiment; not independently reproduced)
evidence.glossary_fit: Illustrative, bounded; does not establish generality

source_locations.SRC-015: Sections 3-5; Appendix B.3, H.1-H.3 and J.1; Tables 2, 5 and 7

evidence.limitations: Prompt/topology interventions sometimes improved results; the GPT-4 AG2 topology gain was nonsignificant (p=0.4). Failures are not inevitable. Taxonomy is not exhaustive; incomplete closed-platform traces prevented detailed annotation. These are benchmark observations, not wild-coordination prevalence.
evidence.open_questions: Root cause cannot safely be inferred from surface missingness alone; transfer to newer systems is untested here.
evidence.support_assessment: Attributed research finding; not independently reproduced by the Commons.
evidence.dispute_status: No explicit correction located in bounded search; not a systematic retraction clearance
evidence.verification_status: Not independently verified by the Commons

terms.name: Assurance
terms.definition: Evidence-supported confidence that specified properties or outcomes will hold under stated objectives, operating conditions, and assumptions. Assurance has a defined scope and can lose relevance when those conditions change.

terms.name: Reference environment integrity
terms.definition: The reliability, provenance, completeness, and resistance to manipulation of information used to make operational or assurance judgments, including documents, logs, telemetry, evidence, and monitoring outputs.

relationships.explanation: Qualifies confidence outside the tested conditions; success or failure is not universal.
Evidence availability, completeness and provenance condition the inference.
